C. Mains, a young man of twenty, running his first race for us, did very well over what is, perhaps, the most difficult stage of the lot, involving, as it does, the gradual ascent of the South Downs, culminating in the climb of Dale Hill.

Owing to the alteration in the course, it is impossible to compare Bert’s time with that of previous years, but undoubtedly it was of a very high order. This running won for Bert the sealed handicap, with Arthur Penny second, and Cecil Mains third.
Frank Webb continued and held our position, although Hallamshire and Surrey A.C. gained on us slightly. Frank's time was fifth fastest, and now came Cecil Mains.
